claimAssessments.reasoning: The strongest record is against: the critical report finds no study identifying a smooth-muscle latch at any tender point and no time-resolved imaging of a release (VASO-E016). The case's own study adds that pressurized skeletal-muscle arterioles show maintained or rising phosphorylation, not the dephosphorylated hold a latch requires (VASO-E020), and that no arteriole's holding cost has ever been measured (VASO-E019). The one supporting record, high-resistance Doppler flow near trigger points (VASO-E027), is weighed at zero diagnosticity because its authors list contracture compression as a co-equal cause. VASO-E013 and VASO-E037 are hypothesis statements; VASO-E044 and VASO-E045 rest on an unread source and are treated as absent. The claim is unresolved, leaning against, and it survives only because every arteriole study held its stimulus on and so could not have seen input-free persistence.

treatment.plainLanguage: A knot is a tiny blood vessel inside the muscle locked shut by its own smooth muscle, starving the tissue around it — not damaged tissue.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: This is the thesis in the form the case grades; if true it decides the case for the vascular account, and if the arteriole cannot latch it forces the vascular idea to the skin or out altogether.
treatment.strongestObjection: Where the arteriole has been examined with the right molecular readout, it shows sustained activation, not a latch; the abnormal vessels imaged near trigger points are conduit-scale and a centimeter away; and the stiff regions measured lie inside the muscle where contracture would put them.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A pressurized skeletal-muscle arteriole holding constriction after its stimulus is withdrawn, at falling phosphorylation and measured low energetic cost (VASO-R004).
A palpated knot stiff on elastography and active on EMG yet metabolically cold on FDG-PET (VASO-R013).
Against it: a hot knot on PET, the non-latching motor-protein phenotype throughout skeletal-muscle arterioles, or releases equal at sham sites.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Held on its anchor alone, in a source (SRC-JHONG-2026A) the ledger has not been able to read; no admitted evidence record bears on it in either direction. It is featured because it is a genuinely different mechanism with cheap tests, not because anything supports it.

treatment.plainLanguage: On the skin-vessel picture, three things hold a knot at once: the vessel's own tone, a collar of gelled lubricant around the bundle, and the tether that collar makes between the fascial sheet and the tissue beneath.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: If shown, it would relocate the vascular account to a compartment where it can be filmed and would absorb pressure-alone release; with no evidence it decides nothing yet.
treatment.strongestObjection: The graded stiff regions blinded sonographers measured in two muscles lie inside the muscle, not in the fascia under the skin, and the account has nothing behind it but its proponent's unread essay.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Blinded tender points coinciding with pencil-Doppler-mapped perforators above chance (VASO-R015).
A knot released by saline hydrodissection at its perforator with no breath or pressure (VASO-R017).
A null on the coincidence map, which would return the vascular idea to the muscle or dissolve it.

claimAssessments.reasoning: The only record is the founding essay's uncited assertion that the traditional maps place the important knots along the torso midline and limbs (VASO-E039), with no coding rule and no chance baseline. The critical report's requirement for blinded coding stands unmet; nothing supports or refutes the claim.

treatment.plainLanguage: The knots and channels described by Tibetan, Indian and Chinese contemplative traditions are first-person maps of the same body system, drawn by people trained to feel their insides.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Even a genuine alignment of traditional knot locations with vascular geography would not show that anything latches or clenches; it would make the maps admissible documents, not decide the mechanism.
treatment.strongestObjection: Correspondence found after the fact is the weakest kind of evidence; without preregistered coding every match is vulnerable to post-hoc selection.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Preregistered anatomical coding of rtsa mdud, granthi and ashi locations aligning with vascular branch points, sympathetic chains or fascial perforations above chance (VASO-R006).
The same coding finding no alignment above chance.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Hai and Murphy's kinetic model reproduces high sustained stress at low myosin phosphorylation in vascular smooth-muscle preparations (VASO-E003); this is textbook physiology. The case's study qualifies its reach: latch behaviour was present in a parent conduit artery and absent in its own downstream branch, attributed to motor-protein isoforms, and never followed into arterioles (VASO-E021). The essay's restatement (VASO-E034) overstates the model — low activation, not none.

treatment.plainLanguage: Smooth muscle in vessel walls can lock its grip and hold tension cheaply after the signal that started it fades.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: A capability, not an observation at a knot; conventional physiology holds it too, so it decides nothing between the accounts until it is shown in the vessel a knot would need.
treatment.strongestObjection: The latch is not generic across vascular smooth muscle, and the one comparison down a vessel tree lost it one branch order later.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A paired-caliber study showing latch capacity persisting into skeletal-muscle arterioles would extend the claim's reach to where the thesis needs it.
The non-latching phenotype throughout arterioles would confine the claim to conduit vessels.

claimAssessments.reasoning: This is a conditional inference graded on physiological priors — structural remodeling takes days to weeks — rather than on any time-resolved record; the essay states the argument (VASO-E035), and the only imaged change attached to the claim is over visits after needling (VASO-E030). Its premise, an objective seconds-scale event, is unmeasured; the runners' study recorded on VASO-C039 shows an imaged stiff focus vanishing within a session under pressure, which is minutes, not seconds, and is state-not-scar without being vascular.

treatment.plainLanguage: If a tender point really lets go in seconds, whatever let go was something the body was actively doing, not scar tissue.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Separates state from scar, which all three live accounts already accept; it does not separate vascular from guarding or densification.
treatment.strongestObjection: 'State' is a bigger tent than 'vascular': sustained motor guarding and thinned fascial lubricant are both states that could reverse fast.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Time-resolved imaging of a felt release showing a local stiffness drop within seconds (VASO-R001).
A retrieved densification timescale showing reversal within seconds under pressure with no perfusion change (VASO-R008).

claimAssessments.reasoning: Held on its anchor alone — the essay's attribution of the densification model to the Stecco group — with no admitted evidence record; the primary literature and the reversal timescale have not been retrieved.

treatment.plainLanguage: The gluey lubricant between fascial layers can thicken and then thin again under pressure, movement and warmth.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: A fast, non-vascular state mechanism; if densification reverses within a session under pressure, the vascular accounts lose their claim to be the only fast mechanism, and pressure-alone release is exactly what it predicts.
treatment.strongestObjection: The critical report finds no direct demonstration that a painful trigger point consists of reversible hyaluronan aggregation, and no timescale has been measured.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A retrieved primary reporting hyaluronan viscosity or fascial glide reversing under load and warmth, with its timescale (VASO-R008).
Imaging of a release showing stiffness falling with no perfusion change.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Physiological blood-pressure pulsations modulate central neuronal activity through mechanosensitive channels in rat preparations and awake animals (VASO-E005), demonstrating the causal direction the hemo-neural hypothesis (VASO-E004) proposed. One preparation, brain rather than periphery, and instantaneous modulation rather than storage.

treatment.plainLanguage: The state of nearby blood vessels can change what neurons do.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Necessary for the read path of the memory thesis but far from sufficient; showing vessels nudge neurons now is not showing they store anything.
treatment.strongestObjection: Demonstrated in rat brain on fast timescales; nothing shows it in peripheral tender points or with any history dependence.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A peripheral demonstration at sensory endings adjacent to vessels.
History-dependent neural bias from vascular state with oxygenation clamped (VASO-R005).

claimAssessments.reasoning: A systematic review of slow-breathing studies in healthy humans documents reproducible increases in heart-rate variability and respiratory sinus arrhythmia (VASO-E009); the essay's restatement (VASO-E036) adds nothing. The evidence is global and cardiac, in people with no tender point in the study.

treatment.plainLanguage: Breathing slowly, with long exhales, reliably shifts the body toward its rest-and-digest setting.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Every account accepts it; the local, site-specific unlatching the thesis adds on top is what has never been measured.
treatment.strongestObjection: A global shift measured on the heart says nothing about a vessel under one tender point.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A local change at a tender point time-locked to the exhale and exceeding the global shift (VASO-R001, VASO-R016).

claimAssessments.reasoning: A systematic review finds manual trigger-point examination not demonstrated reliable or valid, with no accepted reference standard (VASO-E011); the principal peer-reviewed critique argues the construct rests on circular reasoning (VASO-E010); proponent groups concede the point — palpation 'still subjective' (VASO-E029), 'no gold standard technique' and significant inter-observer variability (VASO-E078, VASO-E079) — and in the one study that checked, imaging confirmed 71.5% of palpated spots as trigger points (VASO-E081).

treatment.plainLanguage: Examiners cannot reliably agree where trigger points are, there is no agreed test for what one is, and the whole concept is disputed in the journals.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Undermines the observation base every account shares; it does not favour any mechanism, but it caps how much any palpation-located finding can prove.
treatment.strongestObjection: Imaging confirmed about three-quarters of one examiner's palpated spots and blinded sonographers find graded stiffness at palpated sites, so palpation is imperfect rather than arbitrary; the critique targets the taut-band lesion, not the existence of tenderness.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: An instrumented reference standard with demonstrated inter-examiner reliability.
A census in which imaging-defined foci and palpated points diverge widely.

claimAssessments.reasoning: The claim now has one population record: in a community general-practice survey using the 18-site tender-point exam, two people reporting no pain had eleven or more tender points (VASO-E082), in a subsample selected on reported pain (VASO-E083 is context). The rest is thin — a second-hand 1986 prevalence estimate for a pain syndrome (VASO-E028), the essay's testimony (VASO-E015), a scanner note (VASO-E018) — and the critical report qualifies the ontology of the discrete spot itself (VASO-E012). The essay's medians and distress correlates remain on its anchor.

treatment.plainLanguage: Small, sharply tender spots in muscle and fascia are common in ordinary people.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: The phenomenon all accounts explain; its truth decides nothing between them, but its measurement problem caps everything above it.
treatment.strongestObjection: Fixed-site tenderness testing is not a count of palpable knots, the one survey retrieved was pain-selected, and the reproducibility of the discrete spot is itself disputed.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A knot census with unselected participants, pain-free controls, children and long-term meditators (VASO-R002).
Retrieval of an unselected community tender-point survey with count distributions (VASO-R010).

claimAssessments.reasoning: Hubbard and Berkoff recorded sustained spontaneous activity in a 1–2 mm nidus of every trapezius trigger point and none in adjacent non-tender fibers (VASO-E001). Simons 2002 qualifies the exclusivity: endplate noise appeared at four of eleven non-tender endplate-zone sites and never off the zone, making the signature a prevalence gradient (VASO-E031). Essay restatements (VASO-E043, VASO-E052) add no weight.

treatment.plainLanguage: A trigger point contains a tiny spot of ongoing electrical activity, found more often there than at non-tender spots in the same nerve-supply zone and never outside that zone.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Establishes that something is electrically maintained; but the signature is skeletal-muscle electrophysiology living in the endplate zone, which fits guarding as well as any vascular write.
treatment.strongestObjection: The silent control sites of the original study may simply have lain off the endplate zone; the generator remains contested.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A repeat with a matched endplate-zone control site (VASO-R011).
A retrieved primary showing sympathetic blockade quiets the nidus (VASO-R009).

claimAssessments.reasoning: Mental arithmetic raised EMG at trapezius trigger points while control sites in the same muscle stayed comparatively quiet, in fourteen subjects, without generalized tensing (VASO-E002); the essay's restatement (VASO-E033) adds nothing. Same lineage as VASO-E001, never replicated, no vascular endpoint, and no matched endplate-zone control — an inference from VASO-E031 on the parent claim, stated as such.

treatment.plainLanguage: Giving someone a math test turns up the electrical activity inside one tender point and not a centimeter away.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: The 'write' half of any storage account, caught in motion; but three readings fit it — stress-sensitive endplates, an arteriole write, a skin-territory write — and the needle cannot tell them apart.
treatment.strongestObjection: The control needle may have sat outside the endplate zone, so the stressor may have selected any endplate zone rather than the tender point.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: The trigger point rising and a matched endplate-zone control not rising under arithmetic (VASO-R011).
A localized skin-perfusion fall over the point and not over control skin during the task.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Held on its anchor alone, in a source the ledger has not been able to read; no admitted evidence record bears on it. It is the perforator account's reading of the stressor result recorded on the parent claim (VASO-E002), which measured muscle electrophysiology, not skin perfusion.

treatment.plainLanguage: When stress turns up a trigger point, the brain is doing what it does when you blush or blanch — narrowing skin vessels in one small territory.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: If a mental stressor produced a localized skin-perfusion fall over the tender point and not over control skin, the write mechanism would be vascular and cutaneous; a null would remove the perforator account's explanation of the stressor result.
treatment.strongestObjection: The signal the needle recorded is skeletal-muscle electrophysiology at depth; nothing measured at the skin has ever been reported.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Laser speckle over a tender point during mental arithmetic showing a local perfusion fall absent at control skin.
No local perfusion change, or an equal change at control skin.

claimAssessments.reasoning: The only record is the proponent's first-person report in an AI-generated essay (VASO-E014): testimony consistent with practitioner lore, measured by no one. It is real evidence that people feel a release and no evidence about the tissue. The breath component of the report is now exposed by the pressure-only finding recorded on the child claim VASO-C039.

treatment.plainLanguage: Press into a knot and breathe out slowly, and within seconds it feels as though something lets go.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: The anchor phenomenon of the whole case, but as stated it is a felt event; expectation and global relaxation predict it as well as any vascular account does.
treatment.strongestObjection: Expectation and attention cannot be excluded from any first-person release report, and an imaged trigger point disappeared under pressure with nobody told to breathe.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A local stiffness drop and perfusion rise time-locked to the exhale and button press, absent at sham sites (VASO-R001, VASO-R016).
Felt releases with no reproducible local transition.

claimAssessments.reasoning: The claim's own truth condition makes it false if pressure alone suffices. In the one retrieved study bearing on it, no breathing instruction, recording or manipulation appears anywhere in the methods or results, and thumb compression in thirty-second bouts made about three-quarters of imaged points undetectable after the first course and all but two at 24 hours (VASO-E067, moderate, undermines). No admitted record supports the claim; its anchor is the proponent's essay. Confidence is capped at moderate because breathing was uncontrolled rather than held — a subject under painful pressure may exhale slowly unprompted — the endpoint is detectability rather than a felt release, and the muscle and population differ from the practitioner reports.

treatment.plainLanguage: Pressing on a knot without changing your breathing does not release it — you need the exhale too.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: The breath's necessity is what most cleanly separates an autonomically gated vascular release from guarding that pressure alone can switch off; pressure sufficing removes the cleanest argument that the releasing element answers to autonomic state.
treatment.strongestObjection: 'No breath instruction' is not 'breath held constant': the runners may have exhaled under pressure without being told, and the arm that would exclude it — pressure applied only during an inhale-and-hold — has not been run.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Held breath blocking the clearance that free or slow breathing produces in a breath-randomised repeat (VASO-R020) — which would reopen the claim.
Equal clearance under held breath, closing it.
Release by saline hydrodissection with no breath (VASO-R017), which would confirm the breath is not required.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Held on its anchor alone; no admitted evidence record observes the order of perfusion and stiffness change at a release, and the one imaged fast release in the ledger (on VASO-C039) took no Doppler measurement at all.

treatment.plainLanguage: When a knot releases with the breath, blood flow returns first and the stiffness drops second.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: The one timing prediction the vascular accounts make that guarding and densification do not; observed in either order it would decide between vascular and non-vascular, though not between arteriole and perforator.
treatment.strongestObjection: Both vascular accounts predict it and the conventional account predicts no perfusion change, so it is a test, not yet an observation; nothing has been filmed.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Time-resolved Doppler and elastography showing perfusion leading stiffness across events (VASO-R001).
Stiffness leading, simultaneity, or stiffness falling with no perfusion change.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Acidic, mediator-rich fluid at active points, elevated remotely as well (VASO-E006); blinded-sonographer graded stiffness in the trapezius (VASO-E023); a group-level pulsatility difference (VASO-E022) whose indices cannot classify sites (VASO-E025) and sit inside symptomatic muscle with no pain-free controls (VASO-E026); a second-hand systematic review (VASO-E007). A second laboratory reproduces the stiffness gradient in the calf — active points stiffer relative to surrounding muscle than latent ones (VASO-E071), larger (VASO-E070), more painful (VASO-E069), cleared less often after one round (VASO-E072) — but as active-versus-latent within symptomatic runners, with no control tissue, no Doppler and no biochemistry, which is why those records are context and qualifier. Essay restatements (VASO-E042, VASO-E050, VASO-E051) add no weight.

treatment.plainLanguage: Where a trigger point is, the tissue is measurably different — more acidic, stiffer, and with somewhat different blood flow.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Something is objectively there; but compression by contracted fiber produces the same chemistry and the same flow pattern, and the stiffness says nothing about what the stiff tissue is.
treatment.strongestObjection: No comparison anywhere in the ledger includes pain-free control tissue, the flow indices cannot classify a site, and the mediators were elevated remotely.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A census with pain-free controls in which Doppler-defined and elastography-defined foci coincide with palpated points (VASO-R002).
Imaging in which the differences vanish once palpation is replaced by an instrumented reference.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Preregistered within-subject experiments in 57 volunteers: attending to a histamine skin prick produced about 1.5-fold smaller and faster-resolving responses in about 90% of participants across two cohorts, with no difference in arousal measures and higher heart-rate variability under inward attention (VASO-E008). Single laboratory, published August 2026; the demonstrated route is vagal immune regulation over tens of minutes in a tissue the parasympathetic system does not directly innervate (VASO-E041).

treatment.plainLanguage: Simply paying attention to an inflamed spot on your skin makes the inflammation smaller and shorter, without any change in stress arousal.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: An existence proof that cognition can write to a peripheral vascular bed at a chosen site; it says nothing about knots, smooth muscle or seconds.
treatment.strongestObjection: Tens of minutes, an immune route, one lab, no tender point.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Attention altering perfusion or stiffness at a tender point within seconds.
Independent replication, or failure to replicate.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Median pulsatility index 8.3 near active sites against 3.0 near normal sites, blinded sonographers (VASO-E022); all sites within symptomatic patients, no pain-free controls, and the authors say the findings do not represent normal variation (VASO-E026).

treatment.plainLanguage: Arteries near active trigger points show blood surging and falling more sharply with each heartbeat than arteries near normal spots in the same muscle.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Consistent with something increasing downstream resistance, which contracture, inflammation and transducer pressure all do as readily as a constricted vessel.
treatment.strongestObjection: The variance was so large the index could not classify a single site, and the vessels are conduit-scale, a centimeter or two away.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Pain-free control values for the same vessels.
Microvascular Doppler at the point itself.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Retrograde diastolic flow at 15 of 49 palpably normal sites (31%), against 40% of latent and 55% of active sites, in the same blinded Doppler series (VASO-E022); 'normal' sites were five centimeters from a trigger point in symptomatic muscle (VASO-E026).

treatment.plainLanguage: Blood flowing backward between heartbeats shows up near about a third of spots that feel normal, in people who have trigger points elsewhere in the muscle.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: The finding that turns the Doppler waveform from a marker of a knot into a gradient across symptomatic muscle; it weakens the 'footprint of a clenched vessel' reading whichever account is true.
treatment.strongestObjection: Normal sites near trigger points may show spillover rather than a true baseline; the source cannot say which.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: The retrograde-flow rate in pain-free subjects.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Mean stiff area 0.57, 0.36 and 0.17 cm² at active, latent and normal sites, sonographers blinded to clinical status, AUC 0.9 active against normal (VASO-E023). The calf study is a parallel from another muscle and method — active points stiffer and larger than latent (VASO-E073), cleared less readily (VASO-E074), the authors' conjecture about lesion stage (VASO-E076) and call for controlled confirmation (VASO-E077) — not a replication, and it has no normal sites.

treatment.plainLanguage: The stiff region around a trigger point is largest at painful points, smaller at points that hurt only when pressed, and smallest at normal spots.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: The best-evidenced objective correlate of a palpated knot, and it lies inside the muscle; it fits every account, and its location inside the muscle is a fact the perforator account owes an answer to.
treatment.strongestObjection: One vibration frequency from a handheld massager, sites chosen by palpation, and the same NIH lineage as the chemistry work.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Shear-wave replication with pain-free controls and instrumented site selection.
Failure of the gradient once sites are chosen by imaging rather than palpation.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Endplate noise at four of eleven non-tender endplate-zone sites, against eleven of eleven trigger-point sites (VASO-E032); ten subjects, nonrandomized, unblinded, abstract only, authors are the construct's leading proponents.

treatment.plainLanguage: The faint electrical noise found at trigger points also turns up at some non-tender spots, as long as they lie in the zone where nerves meet the muscle.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Relocates the electrical signature to the endplate zone first and the trigger point second, which is the conventional endplate reading and exposes the missing control in the stressor experiment.
treatment.strongestObjection: Small, unblinded, abstract-only; the prevalence gradient still favours the trigger point.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A blinded repeat with matched endplate-zone controls under a stressor (VASO-R011).

claimAssessments.reasoning: Endplate noise never occurred at taut-band sites outside an electrically located endplate zone, P = 0.000034 (VASO-E032); same small unblinded study.

treatment.plainLanguage: Tight bands of muscle that lie outside the nerve-supply zone show none of the electrical noise.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Ties the electrical signature to endplates rather than to tautness; a taut band without an endplate is electrically silent, which fits a skeletal-endplate generator.
treatment.strongestObjection: Small sample and abstract-only reporting.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Spontaneous activity recorded at off-zone taut-band sites in a larger blinded series.

claimAssessments.reasoning: No differences in resistivity index between active, latent and normal sites, and the pulsatility index too variable to classify (VASO-E024); the authors attribute the similarity partly to the proximity of normal sites to trigger points.

treatment.plainLanguage: One standard measure of downstream blood-flow resistance was the same near trigger points and near normal spots.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: A null vascular index recorded in its own right; it makes the vascular signature partial rather than categorical, which weighs against any account that predicts a throttled bed under every knot.
treatment.strongestObjection: Normal sites within five centimeters of a trigger point in symptomatic muscle may not be normal.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Resistivity index near trigger points compared with pain-free controls.
